lens: F, consistency: brief against brief, and brief against code

findings.title: The layer rule forbids the imports the brief plans for the collector loop and the analysis
findings.evidence: uv run python docs/review/probes/f-consistency/layer_rule.py -> 'collector imports store FAILS (docs/14 store.raw: imported by the collector loop, phase 1)', 'collector imports attribution FAILS', 'attribution imports store FAILS', 'analysis imports store FAILS'. tests/test_layers.py:9-18 puts store, collector, attribution and analysis all at layer 2; tests/test_layers.py:43 requires same package or LAYER[target] < LAYER[package]. docs/14-baseline-modules.md:304 'Imported by: Nothing yet. The collector loop will, in phase 1.'; docs/17-build-prompt.md:269 places 'the collector loop with adaptive cadence and the overhead guard around the existing sampler' in component 07 collector.sampler (docs/13-build-list.md:17); docs/05-data-flow.md:49 'analysis reads windows from the store'; growth.py docstring 'The detectors that call them decide which tier'. docs/17-build-prompt.md:46 'Five layers with data flowing one way: providers, sampler, attribution, store, analysis' contradicts AGENTS.md:37 and LAYER, which give the four one layer.
findings.impact: The first phase-1 task that wires the collector loop inside collector/ (as docs/13, 14 and 17 describe) turns pytest red; detectors in analysis cannot call store.query. A swarm that assigns file ownership by package will plan the loop in a package where it cannot live.
findings.proposed_change: docs/14-baseline-modules.md (the 'How they fit together' figure and the store.raw and store.query 'Imported by' lines) and docs/17-build-prompt.md:46: state that the running loops live in a new package at layer 3 beside cli (for example `daemon`, holding the collector loop and the server's rollup, retention and detector scheduling), added to LAYER in tests/test_layers.py; collector, attribution, store and analysis stay libraries that do not import one another. Propose matching wording for AGENTS.md:37 to the owner. Replace 17's 'five layers' sentence with the AGENTS.md order.
findings.cost: About ten lines across two documents, one proposed line in AGENTS.md and one entry in the LAYER table.
findings.decision_question: Where do the collector loop and the server wiring live? (a) A new layer-3 package beside cli. Recommended: the four layer-2 packages stay independent and the collector stays replaceable. (b) Raise collector to layer 3. (c) Order the layer-2 packages, which needs analysis above store.
findings.refutation_attempt: Searched docs/13 and 14 for any package that would host the loop above layer 2: none; component 07 is collector.sampler and component 20 is server.api. AGENTS.md:37 says to add a new package to LAYER but no document says the loop needs one. Re-read the test: same_package is true only for the same top-level package, so collector->store is refused.

findings.title: The verdict is specified three ways: thresholds, hysteresis, classes and severities differ between docs/02, docs/07, docs/17 and the config
findings.lens: F consistency (brief vs brief, brief vs code)
findings.evidence: docs/02-what-it-looks-like.md:74 'Memory-bound | Serious | Commit above 86%. Stays until it falls below 82%'; :75 'CPU-bound | Warning | CPU time above 86%. Stays until it falls below 80%' (brief.html mock code: 'else if(cp>0.86||(v===\'cpu\'&&cp>0.8))v=\'cpu\''). docs/07-analysis.md:97 'Run queue above 1 per core, CPU time above 85%'; :98 'Commit above 85% of limit, page writes rising', with no hysteresis. docs/02:76-77 'Memory tightening | Warning | Commit above 74%' and 'No bottleneck | Healthy' appear only in 02; docs/07:95-102 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:157 list CPU-bound, memory-bound, I/O-bound, GPU-bound, thermally throttled and inconclusive, with no result for a healthy machine. docs/02:30 the CPU tile 'Turns serious above 86%' while the CPU-bound verdict at the same threshold is a Warning (02:75). docs/08-configuration.md:94 'thresholds.* | see verdict table' does not say which table. src/submeter/core/config.py:143 'thresholds: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)' has no defaults and accepts any key (e-baseline config_cases.out.txt: 'verdict.thresholds.cpu_tyme = 0.85: accepted'), against docs/08:5 'unknown keys are rejected' and docs/14:173 'Unknown keys are errors'.
findings.impact: A builder following 07 or 17 returns Inconclusive, or nothing, on a healthy machine, and 02's steady scenario ('Healthy: No bottleneck') cannot be reproduced. The P3 verdict fixtures have no single source for thresholds. A misspelt threshold silently keeps the default.
findings.proposed_change: docs/07-analysis.md becomes the single source. Add a 'No bottleneck, Healthy' row (all signals below threshold, at least 60 s of data). Give each threshold's default with its release level, for example CPU on at 85% and off at 80%, commit on at 85% and off at 82%. Say whether Memory tightening is a verdict or a finding. docs/02: mark the mock's 86 and 74 as the simulation's own figures, or align them with 07. docs/08:94: 'see the verdict table in docs/07'. Name the threshold keys so that Verdict.thresholds in core/config.py can become a model with fixed fields.
findings.cost: About fifteen lines of documents; about fifteen lines in config.py.
findings.refutation_attempt: docs/07:104 calls the thresholds 'starting points', which explains different numbers but not two tables with different rules, classes and hysteresis; docs/08:94 refers to 'the verdict table' in the singular. Grepped brief.html's mock code to confirm that 86, 80, 82 and 74 are what the mock really uses.

findings.title: docs/03's cost sample labels System as kernel and Restricted as polled, against docs/02 and the code; Restricted memory is 0.3 GB in one and n/a in the other
findings.lens: F consistency (brief vs brief, brief vs code)
findings.evidence: docs/03-cli-output.md:18 'system kernel 0.24 n/a n/a n/a'; :19 'restricted polled 0.05 n/a n/a 14'. docs/02-what-it-looks-like.md:44 '| System | counters |'; :45 '| Restricted | partial | 0.16 | 0.3 GB | 14 |'. core/models.py:28-34 AccountingSource is kernel, polled, counters, partial; attribution/rules.py:213-216 labels restricted 'partial' (doc_vs_code.out.txt: 'restricted source=partial'). Memory: docs/06 metric catalogue 'Memory for totals: USS or PSS' feeds workload totals, and docs/10:17 and 02's restricted tree say other users' USS is not readable. So 02's 0.3 GB can only be a working set added into a 20.8 GB USS total, while 03 shows n/a. docs/03:61 also prints status 'opaque' for vm.guest, which Availability (models.py:22-25) cannot hold (e-baseline interface_cases: refused).
findings.impact: The accounting source is the brief's stated measure of how far a number can be trusted. 'kernel' on System claims exact kernel accounting for a figure that no kernel group measures. A builder copying 03 prints the wrong label, and the memory column either sums incompatible units or hides Restricted.
findings.proposed_change: docs/03-cli-output.md:18-19: 'system counters' and 'restricted partial'. Choose one rule for Restricted memory and state it in docs/06's metric catalogue, for example: 'workload memory totals are USS or PSS; where neither can be read the total is unavailable, and working set is shown separately'. Align 02:45 and 03:19 with that rule. docs/03:61: show 'partial' with the note, or add 'opaque' to Availability in docs/14 and models.py.
findings.cost: Three lines in docs/03 and one sentence in docs/06.
findings.refutation_attempt: Searched for any statement that cost uses different labels from the dashboard: none. The why sample (03:38-41) uses kernel-accounted and polled the way 02 does; only the System and Restricted rows of cost differ.

findings.title: What starts an epoch is stated five ways, and the storage definition makes every adaptive-cadence and overhead-guard change a new epoch
findings.evidence: docs/04-features.md:24 'Every change of settings, rules or hardware starts a new epoch'; docs/08-configuration.md:5 'every change starts a new epoch'; docs/08:116 'Any change to sampling, rules or providers starts a new epoch'; docs/06-storage.md:98 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:130 'the sampling intervals, the rules file, each provider's status, the hardware and the Submeter version'; docs/17:189 'Every effective change starts a new epoch'. src/submeter/store/raw.py:191 'Note something that starts a new epoch: an interval change, a provider falling back.' docs/08:60 adaptive mode 'moves between the active and idle intervals'; docs/08:72 the overhead guard lengthens intervals; docs/08:74 a session overrides the interval. docs/16:257 (R32): a comparison of maxima or percentiles across an interval change is flagged.
findings.impact: If 'sampling intervals' means the effective interval, as raw.py reads it, adaptive mode alone starts an epoch each time the machine goes quiet or busy (idle_after is 60 s), so nearly every day-over-day comparison is flagged and the chart markers become noise. If it means configured settings, it is unclear whether alert, UI or verdict-threshold edits start epochs, and the version trigger is missing from 04 and 08.
findings.proposed_change: docs/06-storage.md, 'When two periods can be compared', copied to docs/04:24, docs/08:116 and docs/17:130,189: 'An epoch changes when a configured sampling setting, the rules file, a provider's status, the hardware or the Submeter version changes. Changes the collector makes itself (adaptive idle and active switching, the overhead guard, a session's interval override) are recorded as events, not epochs, and each bucket records the intervals it used. Alert, interface and verdict settings do not start an epoch.' Align the raw.py record_event docstring.
findings.cost: One paragraph in 06 and one-line edits in 04, 08, 17 and raw.py.
findings.refutation_attempt: Searched docs/ for any sentence that excludes adaptive switching from 'sampling intervals': none, and 08:5's 'every change' includes it. R32 introduced epochs without mentioning adaptive mode.

findings.title: The run file's life is contradictory: two candidate writers for the final totals, 'until read' while the collector still needs it, and no one named to delete it
findings.lens: F consistency (brief vs brief, brief vs code)
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:43 'the launcher writes one file per run'; docs/05-data-flow.md:52 'the launcher one small file per run'; docs/17-build-prompt.md:66: the launcher writes the totals 'when the command ends'; docs/17:67 'something has to keep the group open until it is empty and then save the final totals: a small detached holder, or the collector. Choose one and test it.' docs/16-review-log.md:147 (R15) already settled 'held open by a detached helper'. A collector that saves final totals must write the launcher's file or the server's history, either way breaking AGENTS.md:43. docs/06-storage.md:17 runs/*.json 'Kept for: Until read'; docs/17:68 'The collector finds live groups from the run files... After a restart it re-attaches to every live group'; docs/17:107 'read by the server'. docs/05:44 'registers the group with the collector', while the collector has no API. store/files.py:26 Program = Literal['collector', 'server'], so the launcher and holder have no lock, and nothing deletes runs/ (files.py has runs_dir and no expiry for it).
findings.impact: Deleting on 'read' can remove the file a restarted collector needs to re-attach, or remove it before the final totals arrive. Either way a run's exact cost is lost or written twice (job 1; the P2 gate requires that 'its final totals survive its exit').
findings.proposed_change: docs/06-storage.md runs row and docs/17-build-prompt.md:67,107: 'The launcher writes the run file when the group is created (state live) and writes its final totals when the group empties (state final). When the command leaves processes behind, a detached copy of the launcher holds the group and writes the final state. The collector never writes it. The server copies a final run file into history's run table and then deletes it. The server is the only program that deletes another program's closed files, which also covers raw files under retention.' docs/05:44: 'records the group in a run file, where the collector finds it'.
findings.decision_question: Who holds a group that outlives its command? (a) A detached launcher process. Recommended: it matches R15 and keeps one writer per file. (b) The collector, which then needs a durable file of its own for final totals, because it may write neither the run file nor history.
findings.refutation_attempt: Read R15 (16:147): it settles on a detached helper, so 17's 'or the collector' reopens a settled choice and is the defect. Searched docs and code for a deleter of runs/: none.

findings.title: The 13 API routes serve neither cost nor runs, and the commands that change server state have no route, while POST /sessions is 'the only write'
findings.evidence: docs/13-build-list.md:71-83 lists health, capabilities, config, epochs, workloads, workloads/{id}/processes, series, verdict, findings, diff, sessions (GET and POST) and WS live. docs/13:59 'cost cost per workload, session or run'; docs/16:219 (R26) '`cost` and `diff` read the summaries'; docs/13:35 mcp serves 'cost, findings, verdict'; docs/15:33 P6 gate 'an agent can retrieve its own cost for a session'; docs/05:50 routes every CLI command through the API. No route returns session_summary or run rows. docs/13:64 'config ... reload | rotate-token' and :66 'store ... backup' act on server-written files (token at docs/06:20, backups at docs/06:16), yet docs/13:30, docs/13:82 and docs/17:254 allow no write except session markers. 'session stop' needs its own write. The R05 fix (16:81, 'The ingest API accepts a second collector') and docs/17:79 have no route, and 'the only write' rules one out.
findings.impact: `cost`, the MCP cost query and the P6 gate have nothing to call. `config rotate-token` and `store backup` can only work if the CLI writes server-owned files (a second writer) or uses a channel the brief never states. Phase 7 has no path in.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md API routes and docs/17-build-prompt.md:254: add GET /cost (a session, run or period, from stored summaries) and GET /runs. State that session start and stop are both POST /sessions, or add PATCH /sessions/{id}. Add POST /config/reload, POST /token/rotate and POST /backups as local administrative writes, or say how these commands signal the server. Reserve an ingest route for phase 7, or mark R05's ingest as not in version 1. Update '13 API routes' in docs/13:5 and docs/README.md.
findings.cost: About ten lines in 13 and 17, plus the two counts.
findings.refutation_attempt: Considered GET /series for cost: it answers from rollup tiers, while R26 says cost reads the stored summaries. Considered GET /sessions: it covers sessions, not runs. Considered the CLI reading history.db directly: 05:50 and the 05 figure route the CLI through the API.

findings.title: include_children is used by the sample rules but defined nowhere, and under the default inherit_from_parent = true it changes nothing
findings.evidence: docs/08-configuration.md:232,238,244 set include_children = true on three rules and omit it on 'opaque:wsl' and 'builds'. No document defines it: grep finds it only in the sample. attribution/rules.py:181 'inheritable=self._inherit or rule.include_children'. doc_vs_code.out.txt section 3: 'include_children=False inherit_from_parent=True -> git is builds'; 'include_children=True inherit_from_parent=False -> git is builds'; only False with False gives 'unattributed'. docs/08:101 'inherit_from_parent | true | Turn off to see helper processes on their own'.
findings.impact: A rule that omits include_children, as the sample's builds rule does, still claims every child. Turning inherit_from_parent off, as 08 advises, still leaves inheritance on for the rules that set the flag. CPU and memory move between workloads with no visible reason.
findings.proposed_change: docs/08-configuration.md, under 'Sample rules.toml', and the attribution entry in docs/14: 'include_children decides whether processes started by a matched process inherit its workload; a rule that omits it uses attribution.inherit_from_parent.' In the code, make Rule.include_children a bool | None defaulting to None, set inheritable = rule.include_children when it is set and self._inherit otherwise, and add one test.
findings.cost: Two sentences of documents, about five lines of code and one test.
findings.decision_question: Should a rule's include_children override the global setting (recommended), or should include_children be removed, leaving only inherit_from_parent?
findings.refutation_attempt: Searched docs/ for include_children and 'with children': only the sample and the tree footers at 02. No test covers a rule with include_children=False under inheritance; e-baseline's attribution_cases uses only True.

findings.title: Linux child-time recovery is optional in docs/05 and required in docs/17, and docs/10 and docs/17 state the polled undercount as Windows-only
findings.evidence: docs/05-data-flow.md:65 'On Linux part of the gap can be recovered from the parent's child-time counters. On Windows it cannot.' docs/17-build-prompt.md:71 'On Linux, recover reaped children's CPU time from the parent's child-time counters.' (a requirement). docs/10-known-limits.md:10 'undercounted on Windows, by about 70%'; docs/17:221 'Polled workloads on Windows undercount short-lived children.'; docs/03:22 'polled workloads may undercount short-lived children' (no platform). Lens A measured on this machine (a-linux/child_times.out.txt): 'grandchild orphaned... parent's counter shows 0.00 s; adopted by systemd'; 'child ended while the parent ignores SIGCHLD: parent's counter shows 0.00 s'; 'polling plus the parent's counter: 19.85 s (+50%)' against a truth of 13.23 s.
findings.impact: Following 17 adds child time with no rule for which workload receives it (the reaping parent's, which may be another workload or the user's systemd) and no rule for removing the share polling already credited, so Linux totals can come out 50% high. Following 10, the Linux view omits the undercount warning that 05's 'part' implies.
findings.proposed_change: docs/10-known-limits.md:10 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:221: 'undercounted on Windows, and on Linux wherever the parent does not wait for its children'. docs/17:71: use 05's wording and add 'credit recovered child time only to the reaping parent's workload, and only the part polling did not already credit to the child', or drop the recovery from version 1.
findings.refutation_attempt: Under docs/README's 'which file wins', topic file 05 is binding, so 17's stronger wording is the defect. R01 covers polling's blindness, not this recovery rule.

findings.title: The overhead budget covers the collector in some places and the collector plus server in others, the memory budget exists only in docs/17, and the Submeter workload holds only one pid
findings.lens: F consistency (brief vs brief, brief vs code)
findings.evidence: docs/08-configuration.md:140 'overhead_fraction | submeter | The collector's CPU time as a share of one core'; docs/08:33 'until the collector is back under 3%'; docs/08:22 'Collector overhead ... plus 0.2 points for the store and the API' (the API is the server's). docs/17-build-prompt.md:230 'The monitor must not become the problem ... under 1% of one core at idle cadence, under 3% at active cadence, and under 150 MB of memory across collector and server'. stated_twice.out.txt finds 150 MB only at 17:230; docs/11:22's 80 MB is the Rust switching rule. docs/15:13 P1 gate 'stays inside the budget' names no budget. attribution/rules.py:124,174: Attributor(self_pid=...) claims a single pid for 'submeter'. docs/04:17 'Submeter itself always shown'.
findings.impact: The P1 soak gate cannot be judged without knowing which processes and which memory figure count. The server's rollup, analysis and API CPU lands in Unattributed and in no budget, so Submeter under-reports its own cost and the 'submeter over budget' alert ignores the server.
findings.proposed_change: docs/08-configuration.md (after overhead_limit) and the P1 gate in docs/15: 'The budget covers every Submeter process (collector, server, launcher holders): CPU summed over them stays under 1% of one core at idle cadence and 3% at active cadence, and memory stays under 150 MB unique set size across collector and server. The guard acts on the collector; overhead_fraction reports the total.' In docs/14's attribution entry: the submeter workload claims every Submeter process, not one pid.
findings.cost: Three sentences in 08 and 15, one in 14.
findings.refutation_attempt: Searched the topic files for a memory budget: the only figure is 11:22's 80 MB, which is a switching rule rather than a budget.

findings.title: 'Idle' and 'active' for baselines are never defined, and the usual-range window is stated two ways
findings.evidence: docs/16-review-log.md:121 (R11) and docs/17-build-prompt.md:156 'keep baselines separately for idle and active states'; docs/04-features.md:30; docs/06-storage.md:39 'Active seconds, so idle and busy periods can be compared separately'. No document says what makes a minute or a day idle or active. Three candidates exist: docs/08:64 idle_after (machine quiet for 60 s), docs/08:65 hot_cpu_threshold 0.5% (per process), and store/rollup.py:37,68 active_share = 0.005 cores per series, a constant tied to no setting. docs/07:33-36 shows one baseline of daily peak memory with no split. The window: docs/07:36 'the median of the last 14 values that were not flagged', against docs/06:65 '14 d back' and docs/17:156 'over a trailing 14 days'; these differ once flagged days are excluded. analysis/growth.py:265 usual_range min_values=5, against docs/07:35's 7-day learning period.
findings.impact: Two builders will split idle and active differently, so no fixture can specify the baseline anomaly detector (job 3). The R11 false-alarm fix depends on this split.
findings.proposed_change: docs/07-analysis.md, baseline section: define the state, for example 'a minute bucket is active when active_s is at least half of covered_s, where a sample is active when the workload uses at least hot_cpu_threshold of one core; a day's active value comes from active minutes only'. Tie rollup.py's active_share to sampling.hot_cpu_threshold. State one window rule, such as the last 14 unflagged daily values within the minute tier's 30 days, and set min_values to the learning period.
findings.cost: Four sentences in 07 and one line in rollup.py.
findings.refutation_attempt: Grepped for 'active' across docs/: it appears only in interval names and 'active seconds'. config.py has no baseline-state setting.

findings.title: Behaviours named once and never specified: profile selection, quiet_hours, dashboard token delivery, sessions never stopped, group membership, kernel totals against polled sums, the System bucket
findings.evidence: Profile: docs/08-configuration.md:117 'Each machine can carry a named profile'; core/config.py:280 load_settings(profile=...) is the only selector, cli.py:111 offers --profile on config show alone, and config.py:267 skips SUBMETER_PROFILE (no '__'). Nothing says what selects the profile for the collector and server. quiet_hours: docs/08:98 'off | Hold notifications overnight'; config.py:173 'quiet_hours: str | None', with no format or validation. Dashboard token: docs/17-build-prompt.md:148 requires a token on every HTTP and WebSocket request, and docs/06:20 keeps it in a file readable only by the user; nothing says how the browser page gets it. Sessions: docs/04 says sessions are summarised 'when they end'; nothing covers a session never stopped (crash, reboot), overlapping sessions, or a session during collector downtime. Group membership: rules.py:133 takes a `tagged` map, but no document says how the collector learns which processes are in a Job Object or cgroup (docs/13:24 providers.group reads totals only). Kernel against polled: rules.py:213-216 labels a tagged workload 'kernel' while summing polled processes (e-baseline attribution_cases section 3). System: docs/02:173 'Kernel time, interrupts, deferred calls' and docs/17:97; rules.py:36 SYSTEM is never produced (doc_vs_code.out.txt: 'a system row is produced: False'); b-measurement reconcile_terms.out.txt: 'System as a remainder ... the invariant is exact by definition'.
findings.impact: Each is a point where a builder must guess. The last three decide whether job 1's numbers and the 2% reconciliation check mean anything.
findings.proposed_change: One sentence each. docs/08 'How configuration behaves': 'The profile is chosen by SUBMETER_PROFILE, else the profile named after the host name, else none.' docs/08 Alerts: quiet_hours = "22:00-07:00" in local time, validated. docs/06 or 17: how the dashboard obtains the token, for example a `submeter open` command that passes a one-time code exchanged for an HttpOnly cookie. docs/04 or 06: 'a session with no stop is closed at its last covered sample before a gap and summarised then; sessions may overlap'. docs/05: 'membership comes from /proc/PID/cgroup on Linux and the job's process list on Windows; a tagged workload's CPU, memory and I/O are the group's kernel deltas, and its polled processes feed only the tree view'. docs/02 and 17: define System from counters (interrupt and DPC time, kernel threads, the System process) and report the remainder as a separate 'unaccounted' term, so the 2% check can fail.
findings.refutation_attempt: Grepped docs/ for profile, quiet_hours, token, session and cgroup membership: each appears only at the cited lines. The System derivation is also in the lead's own notes (lead 1); included here only as a spec gap.

findings.title: docs/17 adds requirements the topic files lack and drops others, so the compact spec and the topic files describe different builds
findings.evidence: stated_twice.out.txt. Present only in 17: 17:230 memory under 150 MB; 17:138 synchronous=NORMAL (raw.py:70 uses it; topic files say only 'at most 5 seconds', 16:281); 17:123 'Rollups are idempotent ... A bucket is final 30 seconds after it ends'; 17:69 'Do not allow breakaway and do not set kill-on-close'; 17:146 'Restrict every data file and the API token to the current user' (06:20 restricts only the token); 17:140 'readers accept the current and previous versions'; 17:148 MCP must never return 'command lines or working directories' (08:125, 05:50 and 16:75 say command lines); 17:96 rules match a 'parent chain' (08:217, 14:261 and rules.py:80-83 match only the immediate parent); 17:154 'Track growth at workload level too'. Changed: 17:148 'check Origin on the WebSocket' only, against 15:25's P4 gate ('requests ... with a foreign Origin are refused'), 13:30 and 16:75. Dropped: 17:216-226 known limits omit 10's Restricted and per-process VRAM rows; 17:274 P6 gate omits 'an agent can retrieve its own cost' (15:33); 17:275 phase 7 has no gate (15:37); 17:212 omits the settings view (13:31); 17:94 attribution order omits 'Submeter itself' (14:259, rules.py:174).
findings.impact: docs/README.md 'Which file wins' says the topic files win and any difference is a defect. A builder or cold-read agent working from 17 (prompts/README.md says it 'can start a single-session build on its own') checks Origin only on the WebSocket and fails the P4 gate, or builds parent-chain matching that the code lacks. Requirements that exist only in 17 (memory budget, breakaway, file permissions) disappear from a plan built from the topic files.
findings.proposed_change: Write each 17-only item into its topic file or delete it from 17: docs/06 for synchronous, bucket finality, idempotence, file permissions and schema versions; docs/13 or 05 for breakaway and kill-on-close; docs/08 'Fixed on purpose' for what MCP withholds; docs/08's rules paragraph for parent matching, choosing 'immediate parent' to match the code; docs/07 for workload-level growth; docs/15 for the memory budget. Change docs/17:148 to 'check Host and Origin on every HTTP and WebSocket request'. Copy the missing limits and gates into 17.
findings.refutation_attempt: For each item, grepped docs/01 to 16 with stated_twice.py: no topic-file line states any of the 17-only items. On Origin, R04 gives no scope and the gate covers all requests, so 17 is the narrow statement.

findings.title: AGENTS.md's 'unavailable, never zero' rule is broken by the baseline: unreadable CPU, memory and I/O become 0
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:44 'A metric the system cannot deliver is reported as unavailable, never as zero'; docs/09:5 says the same. providers/psutil_provider.py:65-66 'except psutil.AccessDenied: cpu_s, memory_bytes, threads, restricted = 0.0, 0, 0, True'; :104-110 a denied process gets started=0.0, cpu 0 and memory 0. core/models.py:79,82: cpu_s and memory_bytes are required numbers. attribution/rules.py:208-209 'io_read_bytes or 0'; the WorkloadSample I/O fields are int. doc_vs_code.out.txt section 5: 'restricted source=partial cpu_s=1.0 io_read=0' for a process whose io_read_bytes was None. ground/platform-check.txt: '452 processes, 298 restricted'.
findings.impact: Workload I/O includes zeros for every unreadable process, so the Restricted row shows 0 B/s where it should say unavailable, and a denied CPU read becomes 0 CPU. Those are wrong numbers.
findings.proposed_change: core/models.py: make cpu_s and memory_bytes optional on ProcessCounters and ProcessSample, and the I/O fields optional on WorkloadSample. rules.aggregate keeps None when any member is None, or carries a count of unread members. psutil_provider returns None on AccessDenied. Record the change in docs/14.
findings.cost: About thirty lines plus tests; if store columns push it past fifty, move it to plan.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked whether the brief permits zero for restricted processes: 02's restricted tree and 10's restricted row say CPU time and working set are counted, which is not a licence to write zeros. The same lines are in e-baseline's interface_cases and attribution_cases and in the lead's note 15; reported here once from the AGENTS.md side.

findings.title: The brief requires third-party code that AGENTS.md forbids without approval, and never says the dashboard's chart library is served locally
findings.lens: F consistency (brief vs AGENTS.md, fixed rule 3)
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:46 'There are three at runtime: pydantic, psutil and typer'; pyproject.toml:6-10 agrees. docs/17-build-prompt.md:38 'FastAPI for the local API, with a WebSocket' (which also needs an ASGI server); docs/13-build-list.md:63 and docs/17:142 'export Parquet', which the standard library cannot write; docs/13:35 MCP server; docs/09:13-14 NVML; docs/13:32 desktop notifications. docs/17:39 'Use a canvas chart library such as uPlot'; docs/11:25 'a canvas chart library'. A grep of docs/ for CDN, vendor, bundle and offline finds nothing.
findings.impact: Phase 4 to 6 tasks would stop mid-wave for dependency approval. A dashboard page that loads its chart library from a CDN sends a request off the machine on every load, which breaks fixed rule 3.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13-build-list.md 'Alongside the code' and docs/17:38-39: list the runtime dependencies version 1 expects, for the owner to approve at planning rather than mid-build, and add: 'All dashboard assets, including the chart library and fonts, ship inside the package and are served by the server; the page makes no request to any other host.'
findings.decision_question: Approve a dependency list at planning. Recommendation: FastAPI with uvicorn for the API; JSON-only export in version 1, dropping Parquet; MCP and NVML through the standard library and ctypes; no third-party notification library unless Windows toasts need one.
findings.refutation_attempt: Looked for an approved-dependency list in docs/13 'Alongside the code' and docs/15: none. 17:39's 'served by the server process' covers the page itself, not where the chart library comes from.

findings.title: store/rollup.py builds hourly buckets from minute buckets; docs/05, R13 and docs/17 say from raw data
findings.evidence: src/submeter/store/rollup.py:9-10 'The same functions build minute buckets from raw samples and hourly buckets from minute buckets.' docs/05-data-flow.md:49 'Minute and hourly buckets are both built from raw data', and the caption at 05:52; docs/16:133 (R13) 'Hourly rollups are computed from raw samples while those still exist'; docs/17-build-prompt.md:123 'Build hourly buckets from raw data while it still exists'. docs/14:316 says a test shows 'An hour merged from 60 minute buckets equals the hour built directly from samples'.
findings.impact: R27's mergeable histograms make the minute path exact, so the brief keeps an obsolete dependency on raw files. The server must read raw files for hourly rollups, and those hours fail if the budget trims a raw file (06:117) first.
findings.proposed_change: docs/05-data-flow.md:49,52 and docs/17-build-prompt.md:123: 'Hourly buckets are merged from minute buckets', matching the code and R27. Note in R13 that R27 superseded it.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked whether the merge is exact: docs/14:316 and test_rollups_reproduce_totals_and_percentiles say it is, for sums, mean, extremes and p95.

findings.title: Wording slips that do not change a number
findings.evidence: (1) 'Both programs' at docs/15:46, 17:148 and 17:264, against three programs at 01:29, 05:5 and 13:5; fixed rule 2 says 'Every program'. (2) AGENTS.md:3 and prompts/01-execution-prompt.md:3 say 'a collector, a server and a command line'; docs/13:5 says 'a collector, a server and the launcher'. (3) docs/03:83 and 06:114 say logs come from '2 programs', against 06:19 'Each program'. (4) docs/06:20 and 17:137 'one lock per program so two copies cannot run', while many `submeter run` launchers run at once; files.py:26 Program = collector | server. (5) docs/03:33 'cpu time 91% of capacity' against the reconciled busy share at 03:43-44, 88+1+3+1 = 93 (counts.out.txt). (6) docs/05:73 gives WorkloadSample a 'redacted command', a field models.py:135-147 does not have. (7) docs/04:17 and 17:97 'Submeter itself always shown', while 02's workload table and reconciliation line (02:21) and 03's cost and why omit it; 07's diff includes it. (8) docs/16:107 and 17:77 'parent started before the child', against docs/14:260 'no later than' and rules.py:8,146; the code is right, since start times have tick resolution (doc_vs_code.out.txt section 4: 'child -> agent'). (9) 02's severity names Healthy and Cleared, against models.py:37-41 info, warning, serious, critical. (10) docs/03:5 'Every command also takes --json', against cli.py:108-130 config show and config check (docs/14:367 admits it). (11) docs/17:254 uses a '/api/v1' prefix, docs/13:71-83 none. (12) docs/reference/windows-priorities.md:70 tests suspend with `top --seconds 60`, but sampler.py:39 makes any interval over 30 s a gap, so the check passes whether or not suspend is handled. (13) docs/14:173 'Unknown keys are errors' is false for verdict.thresholds (config.py:143).
findings.impact: Small misreadings for a builder or reviewer. Items 8 and 12 could mislead a test author.
findings.proposed_change: One-line edit each in the file named: 'every program' in 15 and 17; one list of programs everywhere; logs from 'each program' with the figure recomputed; locks only for the collector and server; 03:33 '93%'; drop 'redacted command' from 05:73; show the Submeter row in 02 and 03, or say it is folded into attributed; 'no later than' in 16 and 17; align the severity names; mark the baseline's --json gaps; one route prefix; in windows-priorities, an interval under 30 s that reports the gap flag; 14:173 qualified.
findings.refutation_attempt: Each was checked at both locations with stated_twice.py or counts.py, or by reading the code line cited. None changes a stored or displayed number on its own.
